item: On Windows a merge the timeout killed is rolled back fully once git lets go of its lock (bounded wait, 120 s); a lock still held past the bound is left alone and said
summary: Killing Git for Windows' cmd\git.exe wrapper can leave the real git running and holding .git/index.lock; the helper used to say rollback_incomplete with a half-written tree. Now it waits up to LOCK_RELEASE_WAIT_S (measured basis in the code) for the lock to go, then resets to the old commit (also when that git finished and moved HEAD). A lock with no git process on the machine (psutil) is stale and removed; while any git runs or that cannot be told, the lock is never touched. Release line: On Windows, an update interrupted by its time limit is now rolled back fully when git releases its lock.
